details:
Q1: Which branch should the fix target? The issue body says `stable`, but the cited security-pass script and the `reason=` transfer message are not in this checkout. Agents.md says self-repo review runs take their support scripts from the verified `main` commit.
Choices:
A. `stable`, as the issue body says. Any code that exists only on `main` would be out of reach.
B. `main`, where the review support that ran in runs 37231111364 / 37244083234 / 37251542418 comes from. (RECOMMENDED)
C. PR #6204's head branch.
Q2: How far should the change to `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py` go? The code shows concrete fail-closed rejections that are probably unintended. Line 85 prunes `EXCLUDED` directory names case-sensitively, but `allowed()` (line 38) lowercases them, so `Build/`, `Dist/` or `Coverage/` raise instead of being skipped. Any `.github/<x>` subdirectory other than `workflows`/`actions` (for example `.github/ai`) also raises. So does any directory whose name contains `secret` or `credential`.
Choices:
A. Diagnostic only: report the rejected directory as one of a fixed set of safe categories (for example `case_variant_excluded`, `dot_github_subdir`, `secret_like_name`, `other`) and change no transfer behaviour.
B. A plus the narrow fix for case-variant excluded names: prune them (consistent with the existing "build products are not editor output" rule) instead of raising. All other rejections stay fail-closed. Add a regression test in `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py`. (RECOMMENDED)
C. B plus allowing editor results under `.github/ai/`. **Note:** this widens what the editor can write back to the host, so it needs explicit approval.
Q3: Should this issue also fix the two cycle-five security-pass findings on PR #6204?
Choices:
A. No. Those findings belong to PR #6204's own fix loop (`/re-security-pass` or a fix on that branch). This issue covers only the transfer diagnostic/fix in Q2, and the security-pass gate stays unchanged. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Yes. Also fix the findings on PR #6204's branch. **Note:** the findings are not in the issue or the logs, so planning would first have to fetch them from PR #6204.
